subject.title: Debug capture leaks registered secrets and sentinels retain credential history

question: Should this sensitive debug-capture and sentinel-lifetime hardening be handled in a maintainer/security-owned PR, and what sentinel lifetime contract should replace process-long plaintext maps?
rationale: The issue concerns credential persistence and in-process plaintext retention, and it carries a protected `maintainer` label, so automation should not decide the security boundary or lifetime semantics alone.

options.title: Security-owned hardening PR
options.body: Patch `captureWsEvent` at the persistence boundary and add bounded or request-scoped sentinel lifetime behavior with focused synthetic-secret tests.

options.title: Split capture and sentinel work
options.body: Handle WebSocket capture redaction first, then track sentinel lifetime separately if maintainers want a larger lifecycle design.

options.title: Keep as investigation only
options.body: Leave implementation paused until maintainers define the acceptable memory-retention model for sentinels.

recommendation.title: Security-owned hardening PR
recommendation.body: Patch `captureWsEvent` at the persistence boundary and add bounded or request-scoped sentinel lifetime behavior with focused synthetic-secret tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged sentinel/redaction work and are the live assignee for this security follow-up.
